name: TX-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: San Antonio district with a strong Democratic partisan lean (D+16)
Incumbent Joaquin Castro running for reelection with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger minimally funded with no outside support
Prediction markets price the Democrat near 97%
model.rationale: Castro holds a heavily Democratic San Antonio seat, out-raised his opponent by more than ten to one, and markets price his reelection at roughly 97%, all consistent with a Safe D rating. No polling or expert ratings exist, but the fundamentals leave little room for doubt.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending intervention or an unexpected Castro scandal would be the only plausible route to a competitive race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joaquin Castro seeks another term in a San Antonio-area district that leans Democratic by about 16 points, a margin that has grown in recent cycles. He is a well-known incumbent whose brother Julian Castro formerly served as mayor and in the Cabinet, giving the family deep name recognition in the area.

Republican challenger Edgardo Rafael Baez has raised under $50,000 and has no visible outside support, while Castro has raised over half a million dollars. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available, but prediction markets put Castro's chances near 97%. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being turnout patterns in a low-profile contest.
